close_reason: Fixed: both thisUpdate-in-future checks in OcspChecker now return OcspExpired instead of OcspMalformed for consistent caller semantics
description: pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:180-182 (and :286-288) — when now_unix < thisUpdate, the code returns Err(Error::OcspMalformed). However, OcspExpired is documented as covering 'now < thisUpdate' (clock skew or future-dated response), while OcspMalformed is described as structural invalidity. RFC 6960 §4.2.2 specifies that a thisUpdate in the future indicates the response isn't yet valid — this is an expiry/window condition, not a structural error. Callers parsing error codes to decide whether to retry or hard-fail will get incorrect signals. The fix: map now < thisUpdate to OcspExpired, consistent with the CRL analogues in crl.rs which correctly return CrlExpired for the equivalent condition.
title: OCSP thisUpdate-in-future returns OcspMalformed, not OcspExpired
